validation_rules: Required common catalog fields are validated deterministically
SKU uniqueness is checked within workspace
AI output stays candidate-scoped until explicit user import
Bulk actions are idempotent and return per-record outcomes
permission_behaviors: All launch features require authenticated workspace_owner
No cross-workspace identifiers are accepted without scope check
error_behaviors: Async failures show failed step, reason, retry, and manual fallback
Partial bulk failure keeps successful records committed and exposes failed records

ux_risks: ARCH-RISK-001: scraper failure can interrupt import
ARCH-RISK-004: insufficient queue observability can hide state

keyboard: All actions reachable in logical order
Table selection and bulk toolbar keyboard-operable
Escape closes modal/drawer and returns focus
screen_reader: Every control has an accessible name
Async progress uses polite live region; failures use assertive announcement
Status badges expose text and state, not color alone
Table row context and selection state are announced
focus: Move focus to opened drawer heading
Return focus to trigger on close
Move focus to first invalid field after failed submit
forms_and_errors: Persistent labels, descriptions, and field-level errors
File upload exposes accepted type and size
Confirm destructive bulk actions with count and consequence
visual_and_motion: AA contrast for text and controls
Do not communicate job state by animation alone
risks: Dense tables may be difficult at narrow widths; use stacked records and persistent action access

frontend_task_hints: Build shared job status and recovery patterns first
Keep route handlers/server actions thin; consume domain contracts
Add keyboard and screen-reader tests for discovery bulk actions

ux_decisions.decision: Workspace owner is the only MVP interactive role; AI admin permissions are represented as a workspace settings capability.
Long-running imports use a persistent job status surface and can be left and resumed.
ux_decisions.reason: Stage 3 requires BullMQ jobs and user-visible status.

ux_decisions.decision: Utilitarian visual direction with Bento modular grouping is the recommended design direction.
ux_decisions.reason: The product is a high-frequency operations/catalog tool with dense tables and async status.

ux_decisions.decision: Destructive archive/ignore actions require confirmation; bulk actions report partial success per item.
ux_decisions.reason: Discovery review is a trust boundary before catalog writes.

ux_risks.risk: Users cannot understand long-running import progress
ux_risks.mitigation: Persistent job detail, step timeline, event log, retry/cancel, and partial-result access

ux_risks.risk: AI extraction creates unsafe or duplicate catalog records
ux_risks.mitigation: Discovery Session review gate, deterministic validation, explicit conflict states, no direct AI catalog writes

ux_risks.risk: Dense tables reduce mobile and assistive-technology usability
ux_risks.mitigation: Responsive stacked records, semantic table headers, keyboard selection, live announcements

interaction_tradeoffs: A persistent job surface adds navigation overhead but prevents silent long-running work
Drawer editing preserves list context but requires explicit save/cancel focus management

assumptions_made.decision: Workspace owner is the only MVP interactive role; AI admin permissions are represented as a workspace settings capability.

assumptions_made.reason: Stage 3 requires BullMQ jobs and user-visible status.

assumptions_made.decision: Utilitarian visual direction with Bento modular grouping is the recommended design direction.
assumptions_made.reason: The product is a high-frequency operations/catalog tool with dense tables and async status.

assumptions_made.decision: Destructive archive/ignore actions require confirmation; bulk actions report partial success per item.
assumptions_made.reason: Discovery review is a trust boundary before catalog writes.

stage_decision_brief.recommended_direction: A precise, compact operations workspace: Utilitarian foundation, Bento-style modular overview panels, persistent sidebar, dense searchable tables, explicit async job status, and review-first import flows.
alternatives_considered: Atmospheric AI dashboard: rejected because it weakens dense operational scanning
Marketing-led dashboard: rejected because launch-critical work is import/review/catalog operations
Pure card-only layout: rejected because discovery and catalog require table density
key_decisions: Workspace owner is the MVP role
Website/PDF imports converge on Discovery Session review
Manual entry remains first-class and works with zero AI providers
Async jobs expose progress, retry, cancel, and partial failure recovery
AI never writes directly to catalog

assumptions.decision: Workspace owner is the only MVP interactive role; AI admin permissions are represented as a workspace settings capability.
Long-running imports use a persistent job status surface and can be left and resumed.
assumptions.reason: Stage 3 requires BullMQ jobs and user-visible status.

assumptions.decision: Utilitarian visual direction with Bento modular grouping is the recommended design direction.
assumptions.reason: The product is a high-frequency operations/catalog tool with dense tables and async status.

assumptions.decision: Destructive archive/ignore actions require confirmation; bulk actions report partial success per item.
assumptions.reason: Discovery review is a trust boundary before catalog writes.

risks.risk: Users cannot understand long-running import progress
risks.mitigation: Persistent job detail, step timeline, event log, retry/cancel, and partial-result access

risks.risk: AI extraction creates unsafe or duplicate catalog records
risks.mitigation: Discovery Session review gate, deterministic validation, explicit conflict states, no direct AI catalog writes

risks.risk: Dense tables reduce mobile and assistive-technology usability
risks.mitigation: Responsive stacked records, semantic table headers, keyboard selection, live announcements

downstream_impact: Stage 5 should implement shared data table, bulk toolbar, status timeline, and accessible drawer primitives before page-specific work
Stage 6 must validate async recovery, candidate review gate, tenant-scoped actions, responsive tables, and keyboard behavior
